newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
NEW GUJARAT CHIEF MINISTER TAKES OATH

Shankarsinh Vaghela, head of the Mahagujarat Janata Party (MJP), was sworn in as the new chief minister of Gujarat, after many political, legal and moral hurdles during the past 20 months. Seven more cabinet rank ministers were also sworn in, along with Vaghela, after the Gujarat High Court refusing to grant a stay on his swearing in. Meanwhile, the Bharatiya Janata Party characterised the installation of the MJP government as a very negation of the people's mandate and said the new government would not last long.
Financial Express
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX GAINS 115 POINTS

Pivotal stocks continued to rally on the second consecutive day as the big institutional investors stayed away from the stock market. The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share sensitive index rose 114.73 points to close at 3341.86 on Wednesday. The index has now risen by around 210 points since Friday's close. Analysts said, however, the euphoria created by speculators wanting to lure small investors to the market could be short-lived.
FIAT SET TO INVEST $600 MLN IN INDIA

Fiat Auto is all set to embark on its World Car Project in India. It plans to start the project with two Palio models, the 1000 CC hatchback and the three box Sedan car. Fiat will invest about $600 million within the next two years to set up a manufacturing facility with an annual capacity of 100,000 units.
POWER PROJECTS GET DEEMED EXPORT BENEFITS

The finance ministry has extended export benefits to supplies of capital goods to power projects set up in the country. These benefits will also be available to goods supplied to the oil and gas sectors. Such supplies will be eligible for refund of terminal excise duty as well as special import licences. The finance ministry move has done away with the case-by-case approval of power projects, supplies to which were made eligible for the deemed export benefits.
The Economic Times
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS CUT PLR BY 0.5 PERCENTAGE POINT

The four financial institutions (FIs) have decided to affect a 0.5 percentage point cut in their prime lending rate (PLR). The PLR of three FIs -- Industrial Development Bank of India, Investment Credit and Investment Corp of India and SCICI Ltd -- was reduced to 16.5 percent. The Industrial Finance Corp of India's PLR, which already stands at 16.5 percent, will remain at the same level. The FIs have also decided to reduce their interest rate band by 0.5 percent, from four percentage points above PLR to 3.5 percent.
CENTRAL BANK USING GILTS MARKET TO BENCHMARK YIELD CURVE

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, is using a bullish government securities market to set up an indicative secondary market yield curve in the money markets. By placing dated government securities of various maturities on its price list, the RBI is sending signals as to the secondary market prices on gilts. The central bank has placed five securities with maturities rnnging from four to 10 years on its sale list. These include the zero coupon bond 2000 (third series) at 61.28 rupees, the 13.85 percent 2001 at 100.81 rupees, the 13.82 percent 2000 at 100.54 rupees, the 14 percent 2005 at 102.20 rupees and the 13.85 percent 2006 at 100.71 rupees.
SUGAR DELICENSING, AUTOMATIC APPROVALS MAY BE BACK ON AGENDA

Proposals for delicensing the sugar industry and expanding the list of industries where foreign equity proposals are cleared automatically are likely to be back on the agenda. The industry ministry has sought avenues to make these proposals acceptable. While sugar delicensing was dropped in July after strong opposition from the sugar lobby, despite all ministries agreeing on file, the automatic approval proposal was opposed by the agriculture ministry in September last.
Business Standard
364-DAY BILL YIELDS DIPS 52 BASIS POINTS

The 364-day treasury bill yield dropped 52 basis points at the gilts auction, the biggest drop in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). The yield dropped from 12.65 percent to 12.13 percent. Bids worth a record 12.85 billion rupees were received. In a clear signal to banks to push down interest rates, the Reserve Bank of India accepted only four bids out of 54 received. Dealers said the cut off price of the 364-day bill stood at 89.21 rupees and the weighted average price of the paper stood at 89.23 rupees.
CENTRAL BANK RAISES $600 MLN FROM OPEN MARKET OPERATIONS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, has mopped up more than $600 million through open market operations between September 13 and October 11. Bankers expect foreign exchange reserves to rise further when $370 million of State Bank of India's global depository receipt money flows into the country. As a result of the latest rise, the RBI's total foreign exchange reserves have crossed the $23 billion mark, the highest in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). The last time foreign exchange reserves crossed $23 billion was on October 20, 1995, when they stood at $23.22 billion.
The Observer
EXPORTS OF MANUFACTURED GOODS, CEMENT DROP SHARPLY

Exports of manufactured goods, ores, minerals and cement recorded a sharp drop in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). The slide in the first three commodities pulled down the overall growth in exports to 12 percent during April-July 1996, from 30 percent in the same period in 1995. This was despite a sharp increase in exports of agricultural and allied commodities during the period, which was nearly double the last year's growth rate. The Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy said export growth would slow down to just about 13 percent in 1996/97, against nearly 21 percent in 1995/96.
STOCK HOLDING CORP'S PROFITS DROP SHARPLY

A sharp 42 percent decline in business for the Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd (SHCIL) has led to a severe drop in profits for the corporation in the current fiscal year. This forced the company's directors to lower the dividend from 25 percent in 1994/95 to 20 percent for 1995/96. SHCIL processed business of 82.57 billion rupees during fiscal 1995/96 after 142.73 billion the previous year. The drop was due mainly to sluggishness in the stock market.
Business Line
50 FOREIGN MINING VENTURE PROPOSALS FOR KARNATAKA

The Karnataka government has received nearly 50 applications from foreign joint venture mining companies, including Australian ones. These companies have sought prospecting rights over areas of 1,000-5,000 sq km in the state. The State Advisory Committee is studying the proposals. Of the 277 companies that have put in their applications, 163 are from the private sector.
